summary: Executor start nudge: after each executor clear, dispatch sends the executor one start message whose harness socket ref it passes to executor-start as --sender-ref, until AISDLC-1028 lands

options.description: Dispatch sends each idle executor one start message after every clear; executor passes the harness from= socket ref as --sender-ref; stops when AISDLC-1028 lands
Leave executors idle until AISDLC-1028 lands (drain stalled for hours)
Revert the unchecked-start refusal to a warning (weakens a just-landed control)

body: Since AISDLC-1025 (#1883) executor-start refuses with unchecked-start when neither --sender-pid nor --sender-ref is given. cli-hierarchy clear delivers the executor command by tmux send-keys, which carries no harness envelope, so every normally issued start is refused and the drain is stalled with all five executors idle. The harness stamps a cross-session message from dispatch with from=uds:<dir>/<dispatch-pid>.sock; peer-guard derives the pid from that socket name and compares it with the roster dispatch pid, so a start that passes it as --sender-ref is checked against the roster, not forged. The message carries no assignment: it says only to run executor-start and claim from the board. Structural fix: AISDLC-1028 (clear writes a start token). Class (a): reversible, board-only blast radius, tightens nothing and loosens nothing beyond what the shipped executor command already documents (the uds ref form).
